dedupe_keys.name: gen foam multi physics reactor solver now developed in foamfornuclear

description: GeN-Foam is a multi-physics solver for nuclear reactor analysis built on OpenFOAM. The README read on 2026-09-26 says it solves, coupled or separately, neutronics (point kinetics, diffusion, adjoint diffusion, SP3 and discrete ordinates), one-phase thermal hydraulics in CFD and porous-medium form, two-phase porous-medium thermal hydraulics for sodium and water, sub-scale solid temperatures, and thermal mechanics whose deformations update the meshes. Coverage is mainly coarse-mesh analysis of reactor cores, with pin-by-pin models possible. The code is C++ on the ESI OpenCFD OpenFOAM distribution v2506, with online documentation, Doxygen pages, tutorials and lecture slides from an IAEA e-learning course; it is free under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the GeN-Foam repository is archived and no longer maintained, because development, maintenance and support moved to the foamForNuclear repository; the README also warns that users need Linux, OpenFOAM, C++ and multi-physics nuclear experience. Simulation uses are coupled transient and steady-state studies of reactor cores, for example for safety analysis of advanced reactors, and a physics core for digital twin work. Related records: model-offbeat-fuel-performance comes from the same group and is merging into foamForNuclear, and platform-moose-multiphysics-framework is another multiphysics framework used for reactors.
